title: A finite morphism with closed-immersive fibre is closed-immersive nearby
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and let $s\in S$. Write $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ for the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-weil-residue-field]. If $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], then there exists an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is a closed immersion.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood U of s. Form the section-map cokernel Q and the prime p corresponding to s. Finiteness of f makes Q a finite module. The affine fibre calculation makes κ(p) tensor Q zero.

Mathlib Module.mem_support_iff_nontrivial_residueField_tensorProduct is the Nakayama criterion: p lies outside support Q. Thus Q_p is zero. LinearMap.localizedMap_surjective_iff_subsingleton_localized_coker gives surjectivity of the localized section map, and Module.exists_localizedMap_away_surjective_of_localizedMap_atPrime_surjective produces a outside p with surjective localized map on D(a).
Apply the localized section-map criterion to obtain a closed immersion over S.basicOpen a. The prime avoids a, so fromSpec_preimage_basicOpen and fromSpec_primeIdealOf show this open contains s.

For a finite morphism of schemes, a closed immersion of the fibre extends to a closed immersion on a neighbourhood
